# General static runtime first histories

These four informed studies are not blind benchmarks. They preserve predictions,
original programs, real diagnostics, observer code and observed executable
identities for the corresponding ordinary finite integration. The dirty captures
identify prior executables separately from ongoing implementation. Every quantum
interface has zero or one physical axis; the two-bit ordinary word is classical.
No maximum-size quantum case, sampling or program execution was performed.

The general study retains ten first projects and twelve checks, including two
separate repairs. The first concrete Basis arguments mistakenly used `[Unit]`
and `[Bit]`; both actually refused with the common checker's `type(T)` guidance.
Their untouched first predictions had expected a later finite-profile refusal.
The two separate repairs change only those wrappers and reach that profile
refusal. Seven other generic sources stop at finite Nat/register/profile limits.
These early refusals do not validate original u32 intermediate overflow, checked
helper cancellation, normalized requires, either static arm or the empty fold.
The nongeneric Unit control accepts with 20 native decisions and zero independent
requests; source preservation remains unproved. All original source windows and
both complete observation groups remain separate from those predictions.

The primitive-control study preserves four first checks and 409 Rust source
hashes in every source/executable window. Unused generic scalar-phase and X Ctrl
calls both accept with 18 native decisions and zero independent requests. The X
acceptance contradicts its required sector refusal. The direct scalar-phase call
accepts with one independent request; the direct X call refuses with `contract`
at the original action. Zero-width phase success cannot establish one-bit Ctrl
safety or complete dormant checking.

The derived-phase study retains an unqualified `global_phase_eighth` name
failure, an accepted legacy-source T Meaning comparison, and the exact equation
refusal for scalar `ζ I` masquerading as T. The accepted check reports 23 native
decisions and zero independent requests. Its no-additional-wire prediction,
current derived gate integration and recursive resource checks require separate
implementation validation; these original observations contain no general proof
or binary/source correspondence.

The finite-primitive study retains four actual profile refusals: one-axis
take/put, an ordinary word constructor, an exactly representable phase and an
unsupported sixteenth-turn phase. Both phase sources stop at the original finite
static-argument barrier, so these diagnostics do not establish a downstream exact
coefficient refusal, execution result or rounding policy.

All studies observed HEAD `460f72e019885bd859686b6f4a8b265b40ab36fd`.
The general and primitive-control windows are clean; the derived and finite
studies retain their distinct dirty integration states. The first three use CLI
SHA-256 `0cc0017310561f75f95716603a293065797e370e2be901c26f03aad2f9ae2312`;
the later finite-primitive study uses
`d2ffe826ad0d219dda9e45858d0aa11598945b23c9752848e5dae52f037bfd1c`.
Both are observed prior executables, not a clean commit-to-binary build
attestation. Every selected kernel identity is
`54c9d60b80f67217abd95c8fe6ec1c06aa262e142d5e6db30f46a20cb90faf07`.
Stable hashes identify bytes; they do not attest that the binaries implement the
then-current checked-out source.

Four fixed-metadata USTAR/gzip archives retain all 114 original files / 722,614
bytes: general 61 / 172,127; primitive-control 19 / 525,886; derived-phase 15 /
10,962; finite-primitives 19 / 13,639. `packets.json` binds each original byte
count, SHA-256 and mode-0644 inventory. All 23 original checks remain intact:
five accept and eighteen refuse. The existing per-archive 80-member, 5 MiB
expanded and 2 MiB compressed bounds remain unchanged.

The bounded reader never executes recorded commands, source or observer code and
never extracts archive members to the filesystem. It checks complete inventories,
source/manifest hashes, original prediction/observation order, byte streams and
retained executable/source windows as inert data. This history does not complete
general static instances, the primitive or library cutover, source/native/runtime
preservation, QS/PR/quantitative RS/EXACT, any Issue or a release. Candidate code,
tests, fresh native checking and proofs remain distinct evidence.
